_comment: 英文版数据骨架（v1.0，DESIGN §15）。只存【文案】，不复制结构：
id/part/prereq/figures/demo.id 等结构字段的唯一真相源仍是 modules.json，
这里按 id 引用。结构复制必然漂移（本项目在 figures 清单上已经烧穿过一次），
而『只存文案 + selfcheck 核对 id 集合相等』让漂移在构造上不可能。
status 一律 skeleton：英文正文（content/en/modules/*.html）尚不存在，不许谎称有内容。
闸门同时要求这里的英文文案不得混入汉字——粘贴中文占位是翻译工程最典型的烂尾方式。

intuition.title: Foundations of Intuition
intuition.note: Middle-school maths only. These four are the ground everything else stands on: prediction, surprise, coordinates, descent.

learning.title: How Machines Learn
learning.note: The first time the numbers adjust themselves. Backpropagation is what makes the word 'learning' mean anything here.

transformer.title: The Transformer
transformer.note: The shared skeleton of every current large model. The hardest stretch of the site.

training.title: Training & Emergence
training.note: From 'can continue text' to 'can help': what scale buys, and how human preference shapes behaviour.

inference.title: Inference & Applications
inference.note: What happens once the model runs: how one generation picks a token, reads an image, calls a tool.

safety.title: Capability & Risk
safety.note: The stronger it gets, the more we must ask: how do we know how good it is, and where does it fail?

m01.title: Patterns and Compression
m01.tagline: AI is not 'understanding' - it is predicting the next token
m01.acceptance: Say in your own words why 'model capability ≈ compression quality of the data', and explain why random noise cannot be compressed.

m02.title: Probability, Entropy and Loss
m02.tagline: All learning begins with a wrong guess
m02.acceptance: Hand-compute cross-entropy for three setups; explain what perplexity = 8 actually means.

m03.title: Linear Algebra as Geometry
m03.acceptance: Use a 2-D sketch to explain dot product = similarity, matrix = spatial transform, eigenvector = unchanged direction.

m04.title: Calculus and Optimisation
m04.tagline: Descent: how the gradient points the way
m04.acceptance: Explain what problem SGD, momentum and Adam each solve, rather than reciting formulas.

m05.title: Neural Networks and Backpropagation
m05.tagline: A stack of linear transforms plus a non-linear switch
m05.demoTitle: Build a tiny net, backprop by hand
m05.acceptance: Assemble and train a 2-layer network in the browser to fit a circle; explain how gradients flow back through the computation graph.

m06.title: CNNs, RNNs and the Sequence Bottleneck
m06.acceptance: Contrast CNN receptive fields and RNN unrolled memory for VRAM and serial bottlenecks; say why path length decides gradient decay.

m07.title: Attention and the Transformer
m07.tagline: AI learns to read its context on demand
m07.demoTitle: The attention matrix: where is it actually looking
m07.acceptance: Draw the Transformer data flow on a whiteboard; explain where the O(n²) cost comes from; state how RoPE differs from absolute position encodings.

m08.title: Pretraining and Scaling Laws
m08.tagline: Loss falls as a power law in scale
m08.acceptance: Restate the Chinchilla result (data and parameters should grow together); explain why 'bigger is not always better' looks true and is not.

m09.title: Post-training and Alignment
m09.tagline: Being able to continue text is not being helpful
m09.acceptance: Say why a pretrained model cannot be shipped as-is; explain the SFT → RM → PPO loop; compare the DPO and RLHF trade-offs.

m10.title: Decoding, Sampling and Context
m10.tagline: A model's personality lives in its sampler
m10.acceptance: Explain why code wants temp = 0 while creative writing wants a high temp; name the two reasons long-context 'needle in a haystack' fails.

m11.title: Multimodal Models
m11.tagline: Translating images into tokens the model can read
m11.acceptance: Explain how image-text alignment is trained; name typical failure modes of multimodal models (fine-grained counting, OCR).

m12.title: Agents, Tools and Retrieval
m12.acceptance: Draw the plan → act → observe loop; compare where RAG beats fine-tuning and where it does not; explain why long tasks drift.

m13.title: Safety, Alignment and Evaluation
m13.tagline: How do we know how good it is
m13.acceptance: Name three evaluation failure modes; explain why capability and alignment are orthogonal axes; read a red-team report's structure.
